abstract: A Lean 4 development of the crystallographic restriction in every dimension. For a positive integer m let psi(m) be the sum of phi(p^k) over the prime powers p^k exactly dividing m, except that the prime power 2 contributes 0 (phi is Euler's totient; psi(1) = psi(2) = 0, psi(3) = psi(4) = psi(6) = 2, psi(ab) = psi(a) + psi(b) for coprime a, b; OEIS A080737). Theorem (Vaidyanathaswamy 1928; Hiller 1985; a proof in Kuzmanovich-Pavlichenkov 2002; Theorem 1 of Bamberg-Cairns-Kilminster 2003): for N >= 1, the group GL(N, Z) of invertible integer N x N matrices has an element of order m >= 1 if and only if psi(m) <= N. The development proves both directions: necessity through the minimal polynomial of the matrix over Q, which divides X^m - 1 and is therefore a product of distinct cyclotomic polynomials whose indices have least common multiple m, so that psi(m) is at most its degree; sufficiency by one block of size phi(p^k) for each prime power p^k != 2 of m (multiplication by the root on Z[X]/(Phi_{p^k}) in its power basis), the sign -1 when m is 2 modulo 4, and an identity block. Corollaries: the finite orders of GL(N, Z) are the positive m with psi(m) <= N; the least dimension carrying an element of order m is psi(m), or 1 for m = 2 (OEIS A152455); GL(phi(n), Z) has an element of order n for every n >= 1; the same equivalence holds for GL(N, Q); GL(0, Z) has only the order 1 and the finite orders grow with the dimension; GL(N + 1, Z) has the same finite orders as GL(N, Z) for even N >= 2; the set of finite orders is finite and bounded by 2^(N + 1). The arithmetic of psi: psi(m) = 0 iff m <= 2; psi(p^k) = phi(p^k) for a prime power p^k != 2; additivity on coprime factors; psi <= phi; psi is even; psi as a sum over the exact prime-power divisors; m <= 2^(psi(m) + 1). The tables of finite orders for N = 1, ..., 12 (OEIS A080738) and the largest finite order 2, 6, 12, 30, 60, 120, 210 in dimensions 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 are proved by the bound and a kernel computation of psi. Beyond dimension 12, the eleven orders 2520 (psi = 20), 2310 (psi = 22) and 2184, 2340, 2640, 2730, 2772, 3080, 3960, 4620, 5040 (psi = 24), which rows 20, 22 and 24 of Table 1 of Bamberg-Cairns-Kilminster omit, are checked with their least dimensions. The same equivalence holds in SL(N, Z) for N >= 2 (an element of odd order has determinant 1; the block for 2^k, k >= 2, has even size and determinant 1; -A keeps the determinant in even dimension), and SL(1, Z) is trivial. Every even number is psi(m) for an odd squarefree m (Proposition 3(2) of Bamberg-Cairns-Kilminster and its proof), so for N, M >= 1 the finite orders of GL(N, Z) are among those of GL(M, Z) iff N / 2 <= M / 2 (integer division); each A in GL(N, Z) of finite order m preserves a symmetric integral form, positive definite on integer and real vectors (the proof takes sum_{k<m} (A^k)^T A^k), so psi(m) <= N is also the condition for an element of order m of GL(N, Z) preserving a positive definite integral form; and GL(N, Z) has an element of order m >= 1 and determinant -1 iff m is even and psi(m) + 1 <= N, so the least such dimension is psi(m) + 1 for even m (also over Q). The hypotheses N >= 1 and m >= 1 are necessary and explicit: GL(0, Z) is trivial while psi(2) = 0, and orderOf is 0 at infinite order. The theorem is the standard description of the finite orders of integer matrices, used in the crystallography of higher-dimensional lattices and quasicrystals and in integral representation theory; Mathlib's docs/1000.yaml (Q3527223) and mathlib4 issue #6091 (item 60) list it unformalized, and as of 2026-10-09 no formalization in every dimension, in either direction, was located in the registry, Mathlib, the Lean repositories searched, the Isabelle AFP or arXiv. Not claimed: priority for the two- and three-dimensional cases (public Lean proofs of the case N = 2 exist), the wallpaper or space groups, the isometry group of a given lattice or form, or integral conjugacy.

related_formalizations.note: Prior Lean formalization (SymmetryGraded/Crystallographic.lean: orderOf_mem, no_order_five_or_ge_seven, classification, MA_orderOf_three/four/six; Lean v4.31.0-rc2, no sorry, unregistered, no license file) of the case N = 2: an integer 2 x 2 matrix of finite order has order in {1, 2, 3, 4, 6}, and 3, 4, 6 occur. The tables for N = 2 and N = 3 here are corollaries of the general theorem and are not new. Nothing from it is used.

A second prior Lean formalization of the case N = 2 (lean/Crystal/Wallpaper/Restriction.lean: crystallographic_restriction for GL (Fin 2) Z and IsOfFinOrder, with witnesses of orders 4 and 6; lean/Challenge.lean), prepared for the registry (Apache-2.0 per its formalization.yaml) and not registered as of 2026-10-09. Nothing from it is used.
A Rocq development (MIT, 2026-06-03) of a trace form of the restriction for rotations of Q^3 (orders 1, 2, 3, 4, 6). Adjacent, named in the prior-art statement; nothing from it is used.
